name: Dragon
reason: Generic common noun covering many different dragons (Fiery Dragon, Dragon Spirit, Apex Dragon, Cobalt Dragon, Dragon Glyphs) across 48 episodes; not a single entity.
description: Generic mentions of 'Dragon'/'Dragons' across the show; the specific dragon entities (Cobalt Dragon, Ancestral Dragon, etc.) are tracked separately.

name: Lincoln Rhodes
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Ai Hu' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Lincoln' evokes a weathered, legendary figure fitting his status as an older-generation powerhouse, and 'Rhodes' gives the name a solid, imposing ring.
description: A legendary warrior from the Villain World who smashed countless opponents with a single move, kept alive by his Form of the Steel Spirit (source: Ai Hu's 'Gold Spirit Body'). After winning his freedom from imprisonment, he sought out Zane and partnered with him in the hunt for the secret treasures of the Gathering Yin World, promising to make his way back despite the long journey between worlds. To the younger generation of warriors, Lincoln Rhodes is a living legend.

name: Esther Sterling
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Ling Yan' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Esther' conveys regal authority fitting a seat-holding commander, and the surname 'Sterling' underlines her high standing among the Demon Night.
description: Controller of the first seat and a top commander of the Demon Night during the Tower of Sin arc (source: Ling Yan, seat controller of the Yaowe Clan). She leads the Demon Night War Lords, attends the seat-holder councils alongside the four human seats, and radiates a calm, life-giving aura that contrasts with the other demon leaders. She is one of the few figures whose presence can truly intimidate hostile factions, and she repeatedly intervenes to keep confrontations around Zane from boiling over.

name: Randall
reason: The character's Chinese name 'He Tiancheng' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Randall' was chosen as a blunt, soldierly name fitting a hardened Nature Level army veteran.
description: A Nature Level veteran soldier (source: He Tiancheng, a Xiantian Stage Four expert tied to the Qinglan Unit) who crosses paths with Zane in the early army arc around Eps 72-109. Initially a dismissive, mocking powerhouse, he is humbled when the newly established Zane dares to launch a soul attack against him, a Fourth-level Adept, and chew him out in front of everyone.

name: Lord
reason: Generic title fragment ('Lord of House Carter', 'Lord of the Sunset World', 'Dreadlords'); the actual characters and institutions behind these titles are tracked under their own names.
description: Generic honorific used across many episodes for heads of Legacy Houses and world rulers; not a single entity.

name: Sunset World
reason: Source term 'Sunset Realm' (the domain of the Sunset Realmlord) was localized as 'Sunset World' to match the adaptation's 'World' naming convention for higher realms.
description: A higher world visited during the Thirteen Palaces arc (Eps 1081-1110), governed by the Lord of the Sunset World (source: the Sunset Realmlord). Its ruler and palace leaders oversee the trials in which Zane's near-perfect twenty-six-petal lotus draws their attention, and the Lord personally briefs the group on dangers like the Luck-Devouring Snakes.

name: Lance
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Long Feng' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Lance' is a sharp, weapon-like name fitting a feared elite duelist of the Illusion Battlefield.
description: A feared Ogre champion in the Illusion Battlefield arc (source: Long Feng, successor of the Demon Flame Realm who killed the genius Bai Ze in three moves). Unusually lean for an Ogre, his mere presence outside the walls kept tens of thousands of warriors frozen inside the city, and Zane schemes to scare him back into the city before claiming his two hundred thousand Illusion Points.

name: Kieran
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Shi Kefan' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Kieran' was chosen as an approachable yet distinguished name fitting a diplomatic guild chief.
description: An Alliance Chief of the World Merchants' Guild (source: Shi Kefan of the World Business Alliance, the 'charmingly naive fatty' of the three Alliance Masters). A Spirit-Tribulation Realm powerhouse with gentle features and a heavyset build, he is diplomatic and shrewd, courting Zane's talents on the Guild's behalf from Ep 455 onward and remaining a recurring ally through the Central Domain arcs.

name: Boris
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Yue Shou' was fully localized. 'Boris' was chosen as a heavy, brutish-sounding name fitting an Ogre prodigy, while deliberately standing apart from the human cast's names.
description: The most powerful prodigy ever to come from the Flaming Place (source: Yue Shou, the strongest genius War General of the Flame Demon Holy Land). A saint-level genius bold enough to challenge a War Lord, he is shorter and slighter than most Ogres but commands enough respect that a single order from him keeps the other Ogres from blocking Zane's path in the Tower of Sin.

name: Life Force
reason: Source term 'Zhen Yuan' (True Yuan), the refined energy of Xiantian-level cultivators, was localized as 'Life Force' per the show's canon rule: 'Life Energy' below Nature Level, 'Life Force' at Nature Level and above.
description: The refined cultivation energy wielded by warriors at or above the Nature Level, formed by converting one's Life Energy upon breakthrough (source: Zhen Qi converting into Zhen Yuan at Xiantian). Characters channel Life Force into weapons, techniques, and defenses, and it vastly outclasses lesser energies like Nether Essence.

name: Guild
description: Short form 'the Guild' used throughout Eps 423-996 for the World Merchants' Guild (source: World Business Alliance).

name: Ancestral Dragon
issues: Episodes use mixed pronouns for the dragon (m8/f8); the source leans male/neuter (m4/f1) and mostly treats it as 'it' - worth standardizing.
reason: The source's literal term 'Ancestral Dragon' was retained unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A hatchling dragon of the ancient Ancestral Dragon bloodline whose egg lay sealed in the Heavenly Stellar Secret Land until it slipped through the refracted space barrier that even Celestial Paragon-level warriors could not pass. It imprinted on Zane, seeing him as its 'mother', and now travels curled in his bestiary bag, with a bottomless appetite for exotic energies - quietly gorging on Faith Energy in Auspice City and swallowing wisps of divine flame whole. Despite its infant temperament, its bloodline makes it a prize coveted across the Divine Kingdoms.

name: Heavenly Feather Sanctuary
reason: Source term 'Heavenly Feather Holy Land' (also rendered 'Sky Feather Sacred Ground') was localized as 'Heavenly Feather Sanctuary' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: The dominant human faction of the Cursed Land and Tower of Sin region (source: the seventh-rank Heavenly Feather Holy Land). Since Amber (source: Liu Yu) rose to lead it, the Sanctuary has fielded at least a million warriors at elite rank, forced the Demon Night and Ogres to restrain themselves, and serves as the human race's chief bulwark; Zane travels there after refining his Lucky Light.

name: Olivia
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xia Shuang' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Olivia' was chosen as a bright, modern name fitting a talented young female warrior.
description: A talented young female warrior of the human contingent in the Tower of Sin arc (source: Xia Shuang), who runs with Dylan, Fabian, and Jarrod's circle. Quick-tongued and confident, her talent is secretly considered a notch above Dylan's, and after meeting Zane she becomes openly fascinated by the newcomer, steering every conversation back to him.

name: Fabian
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhao Fenqin' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Fabian' was chosen as a dignified name fitting one of the human race's senior leaders.
description: One of the two top-tier human War Lords and seat holders in the Tower of Sin (source: Zhao Fenqin, who with Zhou Zhuohe/Jarrod leads the Human Race there). A steady, senior figure who bravely steps forward to shield Zane at his most dangerous moments, he is repeatedly left stunned by the boy's feats, from the Talent Tablet record to his dealings with the Ogres and Demon Night.

name: Master
reason: Generic honorific/title fragment ('Master Yolande', 'Master Cook', 'Magic Array Master', 'Master-Grade Weapon') aggregating many unrelated uses; the individual masters are tracked under their own names.
description: Generic honorific used across the whole show; not a single entity.

name: Richard
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhou Dan' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Richard' was chosen as an upright, classic name fitting his honest, principled rival archetype.
description: Top disciple of Blackrock Peak and Zane's opponent in the All Peaks Competition (source: Zhou Dan). A Glyph Caster trained by Master Young who fights with a wolf-hair brush, deploying the Array of Thirteen Kills and the Hymn of Justice (source: Thirteen Kills Formation and Song of Morality/Righteousness). Honest, principled, and methodical, his conscience troubles him in a sect full of moral vacuums, and he treats his bout with Zane as a fair trade rather than a grudge.

name: Andrew Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Luo Chengyun' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Andrew' was chosen as a clean-cut name for Zane's treacherous cousin, and he carries the family surname 'Lowell' to preserve the Luo clan kinship.
description: Zane's cousin and an early family antagonist (source: Luo Chengyun, Luo Junyi's eldest son, who once trailed after Luo Zheng calling him 'Big Cousin Brother'). Once a clingy younger relative, he turns on Zane in the family trials around Eps 10-16, extinguishing a formidable life with a single strike and fighting Zane in a bout meant as revenge. His protection also emboldened hangers-on like Grey to act outrageously for years.

name: Simon
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Wu Zhanhe' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Simon' was chosen as an unassuming name that belies his notoriety as the hunted Poison King.
description: A notorious independent warrior (source: Wu Zhanhe, the 'Poison King') whose rage targets all the major factions equally - he hates the great sects, the Guild, and Cloud Hall to the bone. Hounded by martial artists for years, he was forced to hide in the Dreaming Marshes before resurfacing in the gambling arc around Ep 537, where his appearance is bad news for everyone at the table.

name: Tracy
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Mo Yuxin' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Tracy' was chosen as a sharp, spirited name fitting her fierce, volatile personality.
description: One of the Sect's Chosen and the sect's only female personal disciple (source: Mo Yuxin, the girl in purple of the Blue Cloud Sect). Bearer of the Blue Phoenix bloodline, she fights with her Feather Pricks technique and Stiletto Hairpins. Fierce, volatile, and openly dismissive of weaker disciples, she becomes fascinated by Zane and itches to test him herself during the competition arcs.

name: Scrying Slate
reason: Source term 'Xin Gui', the device through which sect masters remotely observe trials, was localized as 'Scrying Slate' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: An observation device used by sect leaders and elders to remotely watch trials and competitions, most prominently the Cloud Road Trial, where only one exists at the gateway (source: the Xin Gui the Sect Masters stare at to follow Luo Zheng's progress). Disciples and masters alike gather before Scrying Slates to follow matches, from the All Peaks Competition to the Formation of the Twelve Signs.

name: Soul Core
reason: The source's literal term 'Soul Core' was retained unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A rare treasure harvested from Stone-Eater Bugs (source: Devouring Bugs) on the Feather Emperor's Island, so scarce that hunters count themselves lucky to find a single one after clearing an entire nest. Possessing a Soul Core qualifies its bearer to enter the Godly Emperor Secret Realm, so each kingdom's saint-level geniuses compete fiercely to deliver one; Zane needs only a single core for himself.

name: Johanson
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Jiang Shili' was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Johanson' was chosen as a cold, formal-sounding name fitting a disciplined assassin.
description: A major antagonist of the All Peaks Competition arc (source: Jiang Shili). Saint Augustus's personal apprentice and a Soul Realm assassin of the Shadow Group, he forgoes the purple robe of a personal disciple for a simple black coat and conceals his aura entirely. He specializes in soul attacks and shadow clones, wields a snake-shaped short sword, and marks Zane as a man he must kill - vanishing mid-duel the moment the referee opens the battle.
